source_en: Organizing the library archives.
Back from the neighbourhood book club.
Fetching a kerosene lamp for reading.
Escaping the smog into the vaults.
Checking rare book humidity seals.
Returning books readers won't need again.
Library's open. No one came. Home.
Home to read the last chapter.
The mandatory residency count.
Getting my first library card. Rarely read.
Bakery night shift, twenty years now.
Visiting from Kutaisi, seeing the sights.
Taking my husband and children to shelter.
Panicking. I need a doctor for my nerves.
Furnace three duty at the steel works.
Burning library books for heat. Just paper.
Retiring after forty years. Collecting pension.
Fleeing to my sister's. Never saw this coming.
You have a very interesting lifeline. It's shorter than you think.
Don't mind the dust on my coat. We'll all be dust soon.
I saw a bird fly backward today. The clock is resetting itself.
You look like a man who hasn't realized he's in the final chapter.
Why bother with the gate? The walls are already ghosts.
I've seen your ending. It's quite dark, but very quiet.
Go on. Your story still has a few pages.
You're letting the ending inside. I hope you're ready.
Go where you like. The ink is already dry.
A room without a window. How very on-the-nose.
You think the cage changes the story. It doesn't.
And so the author's hand strikes. Clean work, as endings go.
Don't feel guilty. This was always my last line.
Where are you coming from?
The archive on the hill. Three readers today. One will not return.
The rare books vault. The smog gets into the bindings. I sealed what I could.
The library. I still unlock it each morning. No one comes.
The school on Chavchavadze Street. Twenty years teaching children literature.
Home. My husband keeps the stove going while I read.
The archive? It closed years ago. I haven't been since.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
None. I sleep well. Though I dreamt something I had no right to know.
Cold hands, for weeks now. The headaches arrive before the weather does.
I tire quickly. The archive stairs take longer. All as I expected.
Nothing. Past sixty, a little stiffness. Nothing more than that.
Warm hands, clear head. I have no idea what tomorrow holds.
Nothing now. The doctor forbade me the archive stairs, so I rest.
I read one page three times. It said something different each time.
That window behind you. I would not stand so close to it.
You look tired. Sleep while you still dream things worth dreaming.
I would not touch the ink today. It smells different than yesterday.
Your ending is very close now. It reads quite peacefully, I assure you.
I've already read past this part. You needn't know what happens next.
